title: The Centerline-Cross Entropy Loss for Vessel-Like Structure Segmentation: Better Topology Consistency Without Sacrificing Accuracy
mechanism: CE restricted to the label skeleton (recall) and to the predicted skeleton (precision), added to CE. This keeps CE's robustness to noisy annotations, which Dice-based clDice lacks.
adaptation: Crack class only, weight 0.1 to 0.5. The label skeleton is about the 1-2 px trace itself. The predicted-skeleton precision term penalises thin false lines (E1 scuff streaks, gridline confusion) and so counters the widening Skeleton Recall caused.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + clCE (crack, w 0.25), 5 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metrics: clean-49 crack IoU, relF1@2, predicted width, E1 relF1@2. Kill if crack IoU < baseline - 0.012, or width rises > 15% with no relF1@2 gain.
evidence: R (abstract): 2D/3D retinal and coronary data, better overlap than other losses and better connectivity. Exact numbers not read (S2 snippets rate-limited).
prior_overlap: Partial. Soft clDice (Dice-based) failed and Skeleton Recall (recall only) widened predictions. CE-based skeleton terms with a predicted-skeleton precision term are untested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Crack class only, weight 0.25. The predicted-skeleton term penalises thin false lines (E1 scuff streaks, gridline confusions), which should counter the widening seen with Skeleton Recall. Follow the released code; a reviewer flagged sign errors in the paper equations.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + clCE (w 0.25) vs PF, 5 seeds. Kill if crack IoU < PF - 0.012 or predicted width rises > 15% with no relF1@2 gain. Run only if SCNP and TRACE fail.
